subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm deciding to build a pickup truck as a static prop without needing joints, designing it as a hovering vehicle maintained at a fixed height above the ground.

For dimensions, I'm sketching roughly 5.3m long, 2m wide, 1.9m tall, built from boxes and extrusions using imported kit pieces like panelled metal and glow for the thruster pods, with the body chassis, hood, and cab silhouette taking shape through an extruded profile along the vehicle's length.

Defining body and cab geometry...

Computing the tilt angle gives about 40 degrees, so I'll rotate the windshield box accordingly with a thin depth of 0.85, offsetting it slightly off the cab surface so it sits proud. For the side windows I'm sketching a trapezoidal outline in z-y space and extruding it across the cab width so the glass pokes out symmetrically on both sides.

Now I'm placing the rear window as a thin box near the back of the cab, adjusting the cab's rear profile points so the slope reads naturally, then settling on final coordinates for the rear glass slab. For the bed I'm laying out side wall boxes, a tailgate box, and a bulkhead, then adding militarized details like a rail gun, missile pods, a roll bar with lights, armor plates, and side skirts. For the hover pods I'm planning four thruster housings at the wheel corners, built as lathe shapes resembling ducted fan nozzles.

I'm designing each pod as a tapered lathe shell with an outer and inner profile forming a closed loop, adding a glowing cyan disc underneath to suggest a thruster fan, and connecting each pod to the body with a strut arm — checking that the pod height and body bottom overlap sensibly so the pylon mount looks structurally plausible, with the wide pod placement partially tucking under the body's edge for a realistic fender-flare look.

Now I'm planning the small magenta glow rings around each pod base, rear jet nozzles at the back bumper with orange-cyan glowing tips, headlight and light-bar glow elements, and underglow strips along the bottom sides. I'm also thinking through decals — hood stripes, an emblem, door text like "HVR-9" — and working out the correct plane orientation and facing direction so the text reads properly from the side view.

Now I'm designing the body paint: a dark gunmetal base with magenta/cyan cyberpunk accents, layering mottled texture with a countershade for weathering, then wrapping it in a panelled material for the armored look.

I'm working through texel resolution math to decide seam widths and whether rivets will even be visible at the chosen paint sheet size — settling on 2048 resolution and skipping rivets since they'd be too small to read, instead writing a custom plated paint function with seam lines and noise-based wear highlights. I'm also planning hazard stripes for the bumper using a diagonal stripe pattern.

Now I'm settling on the texture list: door decal, grille emblem, hood decal, fan blade disc, license plate, and a hologram dashboard screen, deciding to reuse the same door texture mirrored rather than creating separate left/right versions.

Adding the turret assembly...

Wait, the cab roof sits at height 1.9 with its rear at z=-0.85, so barrels extending past that z-value would clip into the cab—I need to adjust the barrel placement to avoid that collision.

Instead I'm thinking of mounting the turret directly on the cab roof instead, positioning it so barrels extend forward over the hood and clear the windshield entirely, facing forward along +Z.

For the rear bed, I'm adding angled missile pod launchers on either side, tilted upward at 35 degrees, each a box of tubes with a circular grid texture applied to the end face to simulate launch tube openings.

Computing the rotation to tilt the box's z-axis forward by 30 degrees so the tube openings point outward correctly.

Now I'm thinking through extra greebles for the bed area: glowing battery cells or a fusion core made from cylinders, plus copper coolant pipes swept from the cab to the pods using catmull curves for added mechanical detail.

For the front, I'm adding a hazard-striped bumper box, then a plow wedge built from a frustum shape that tapers from wide to narrow as it extends forward, bringing total vehicle length to around 5.7 units. I'm also sketching in a hood scoop and vents for surface detail.

I'm skipping fender flares in favor of angled pylon arms, adding a steel side skirt panel between the pods, and placing a glowing red taillight strip at the rear with twin cylindrical jet housings that end in glowing orange discs.

Now I'm planning the roof details: an alternating magenta/cyan light bar, a roof rack, antenna rods with glowing tips, a lathed satellite dish, and mirror boxes -- skipping wheels entirely since this is a hover vehicle with exposed chassis rails between the pods. I'm also setting up small helper functions for boxes and glow boxes and symmetric placement, keeping the flat color palette under 64 colors, and considering a rotating fan texture for the pods.

Still designing the pod fan disc with glowing cyan blade lines, adding an under-glow ring and gimbal cylinder with nozzle vanes and side lights, and choosing a tarnished iron metal finish for the pod exterior with a lathed satellite dish component.

Checking that the lathe outline doesn't self-intersect and stays positive in x, then working out how the pod connects to the body via a centered arm positioned between the two.

Now I'm placing door panel decals on the lower body region with handle and emblem details, sizing them to fit between the beltline and window, then moving on to the hood shape.

For the hood decal, I'm calculating the slight forward slope of the hood profile and orienting the plane with its normal and up vectors so the texture reads correctly from above, interpolating the y-position along the sloped line from windshield base to front edge.

Now I'm shifting to the grille, computing its leaning normal vector from the front profile points to orient that plane similarly.

Placing twin headlight glow boxes flanking the grille, then sketching angular headlight housings and the face plate dimensions. I'm also marking the roof turret base position above the cab line and adding door mirrors with arm-and-box geometry before starting a reusable plated paint helper function.

Writing plated paint function...

Writing SVG texture designs...

Still writing imports and helpers...

Now I'm positioning the launcher pieces symmetrically on each side, computing tilted box rotations and checking whether the launcher's lower rear corner clips through the bed walls given their height.

Next I'm sketching the roll bar behind the cab as a swept tube over a polyline forming a rounded rectangular arc, positioned relative to the cab bulkhead and roof height, then moving on to defining the bed's side wall boxes with their x-offsets and thickness.

Then I'm laying out the tailgate box, glowing cyan edge strips along the bed rails, and the battery case positioned in the bed center, adjusting the launcher x-offsets to avoid overlapping with the battery housing.

Adding glowing battery cylinders on top, then building the turret with a pedestal base, head box, twin barrels extending forward, a muzzle brake, barrel shroud, and a magenta sensor eye on the front.
